about.summary: Buy when the price closes above its highest high of the previous 20 days (a breakout); sell when it closes below the lowest low of the previous 10 days, or falls 2 ATRs below the entry price.
about.style: Breakout / trend following · weeks to months · low win rate, big winners
about.why: These are the core rules of the "Turtle" traders, whom Richard Dennis and William Eckhardt taught in 1983 to test whether trading could be learned; the group went on to earn large profits. Curtis Faith, one of the Turtles, published the full rules. The idea: big trends start with new highs, so buy strength, cut losers quickly (2 ATR stop) and let winners run.
about.caveats: Built for a diversified portfolio of futures markets, not one stock. Most breakouts fail, so expect many small losses (win rates around 30-40% are normal) and long flat periods, paid for by a few large trends. Results on a single stock vary a lot.
references: Faith, C. (2007). Way of the Turtle. McGraw-Hill.
Covel, M. W. (2007). The Complete TurtleTrader. HarperBusiness.
Wilder, J. W. (1978). New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems. Trend Research.
